## Upstream README

# rasnikism

## Rasniki archive and kerot specification

Read [troubleshooting and practical guidance](guidance.html) for execution states, drivers, revisions, templates, Python tools, and encoded publications.

[Jerry Pop](jerry-pop.html) runs actual K0 programs in a browser with selectable simulated port drivers. The Python software host supports the same attachable devices. See [port behavior and hardware limits](DRIVERS.md).

Jerry Pop also supports [reinterpretable source revisions](REINTERPRETATION.md): edit, reinterpret on a fresh machine, replay a retained revision, and export program history.

Use [templates and editable atemple variants](TEMPLATES.md) in Jerry Pop for reusable greeting, input, branch, and attached-driver programs.

The [executable kerot final-quilt edition](language.html) publishes actual `.kerot` source and `.k0` bytecode, with eight precisely scoped modes and a Python host runner. See [scope and exact checks](QUILT.md). This is separate from the encoded document publication.

The separate document publication uses the [encoded I/O reader](publication.html), with three `.io` edition scripts under `encoded/`. It includes source documents, software sources, interfaces, tests, and license records. See [the I/O format](IO_PUBLICATION.md). Markdown is retained for editorial maintenance; executable target artifacts are published directly under `language/`.

Start with [Ostar Rawful Lair](ostar.html) for the reformatted collection and its Makkakah, Aantonymmakkakah, and Jurisdiction Review editions. See [the edition contract](OSTAR.md). Jurisdiction material remains unreviewed and does not certify legal validity.

This repository contains the Rasniki fictional language and lore, a collection of working local software tools, and a proposed kerot-to-browser architecture. Start with index.html for the collection or catalogue.html for implementation status. Native browser tools require no external dependencies; the K0 host toolchain uses Python 3.

- Open [the archive](index.html) for the searchable glossary, lore, curriculum, and steadings.
- Open [the Immanuel/Emanuel manual and planning studio](manuals.html) for advocacy, rewriting, K0 source generation, blueprints, structures, strategy, and Ostar editions; see [scope and jurisdiction limits](MANUALS.md).
- Open [systematics and reflective voting](systematics.html) for Yorkie, Anticlaw, Blue Esteemer, spiritual sciences, and counterantonymmakkakah definitions with local proposal management; see [rules and limits](SYSTEMATICS.md).
- Play [the Rasniki lair game](game.html) with quests, resources, care, repair, and save files; see [the game API and integration limits](GAME.md).
- Open [Archangel Rawful management](archangel.html) for local profiles, account metadata, publication records, a copyleft checklist, systems definitions, and optional panic support; see [its scope and limits](ARCHANGEL.md).
- Open [the I/O, IAU rune, and IObot editions](io.html) for local text import/export, English-form rune conversion, and deterministic commands; see [their definitions and limits](IO.md).
- Use [searching, matching, finding, summoning, and mathing](search.html) for exact and approximate catalogue matching, selected-workspace links, and exact integer operations; see [the tool's scope](SEARCH.md).
- Open [the ACGI software catalogue and workspace](catalogue.html) for paginated categories, local selection trends, multimedia previews, project drafts, bitflip, and exact integer arithmetic. See [coverage and limitations](CATALOGUE.md).
- Use [the kerot software kit](SOFTWARE.md): an assembler, bounded interpreter, and general, makkakah, aantonymmakkakah, and echo examples.
- Open [the adaptable edition](adaptable.html) for section enable/disable controls and reading settings; see [its definitions and limits](ADAPTABLE.md).
- Read [the existential lair edition](LAIR.md) or its [formatted edition](lair.html), and use the [jurisdiction-aware adaptation tool](jurisdiction.html) for provisional wording and review notes. This tool does not certify legal validity.
- Read [the kerot specification](KEROT.md) for primitive semantics, BIOS/UEFI boot boundaries, Magrigal OS contracts, browser milestones, and acceptance gates.
- Open [the formatted specification](kerot.html) in a browser.
- Read [makkakah and aantonymmakkakah](MAKKAKAH.md) for their proposed definitions, paired lore, practices, curriculum, and steading provisions, or open [the formatted edition](makkakah.html).
- See [development instructions](DEVELOPMENT.md) for local serving and editing.
- Read [books as instruments of repair](BOOKWRITING.md), including nomicest, aimest, sentest, and the literary weapondry, or open [the formatted edition](bookwriting.html).

The architecture is a design, not an implemented operating system or bootable image. Vocabulary is provisional and the material is AI-assisted. The archive uses native HTML, CSS, and JavaScript without external dependencies.
